title.narrative: Enhancing Community Wellbeing through Climate Smart Agriculture, Lifesaving Food and Nutrition Support, and Locally Led Resilience in Borno State.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtltbrgtWith grant support, Concern on Climate Change for the Community Initiative (FOURCi) will address urgent food security, nutrition, and climate resilience needs of vulnerable households in two crisis-affected communities each within Jere and Maiduguri Metropolitan Council (MMC) LGAs of Borno State. These communities face overlapping pressures from protracted conflict, displacement, recurrent flooding, drought, and environmental degradation, which continue to undermine livelihoods and expose women and children to heightened risks of hunger and malnutrition.ltbrgtThe project is aligned with Nigeria’s Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0), which prioritizes climate adaptation, climate-smart agriculture, livelihood protection, early warning systems, and support to vulnerable and conflict-affected populations. In line with these priorities, FOURCi will deliver integrated life-saving and resilience-building assistance that addresses immediate needs while strengthening households’ capacity to cope with climate-related shocks.ltbrgtKey agriculture-supporting activities under the project include: distribution of bio-fortified and drought-tolerant crop seeds provision of climate-resilient agricultural and micro-gardening kits for women training of smallholder farmers on nutrition-sensitive and climate-smart agriculture support for small livestock and aquaculture and introduction of solar drying technologies to reduce post-harvest losses. These interventions will improve food availability, dietary diversity, and sustainable agricultural production. Complementary cash or voucher assistance and the distribution of energy-efficient SAFE stoves will support immediate food access, reduce negative coping strategies, and lower protection and environmental risks associated with fuelwood collection.ltbrgtTo reduce climate risk exposure, the project will implement community-based adaptation measures, including early warning and preparedness activities, community sensitization, and cash-for-work initiatives to rehabilitate drainage channels, protect water points, and strengthen flood-mitigation infrastructure. Farmers Field Schools will further enhance resilience through practical learning on agroforestry, soil restoration, small-scale irrigation, and sustainable natural resource management, with women supported to play leadership roles in climate-resilient livelihoods.ltbrgtIn addition, FOURCi will convene a multi-stakeholder symposium on the link between Climate Change, Natural Resource Management, and Conflict, using the Chad Basin as a case study. The symposium will serve as a learning and policy-dialogue platform, bringing together experts in climate change, conflict, and natural resource governance to analyze how environmental stress and resource scarcity contribute to insecurity. Outcomes will include policy briefs and recommendations to inform resilience-building strategies and support more sustainable, conflict-sensitive natural resource management for communities in the BAY States affected by both Boko Haram conflict and climate change.lt/pgt
